card.name: Words just before a cause-and-effect claim
card.fires_on: Small words (a, is, were, no, definite, prove) right before a word like causal, cause, related or link, in statements that a cause is unproven or uncertain.

modes.label: Unproven causation
modes.description: Words like definite or prove before 'cause and effect relationship' in sentences saying evidence is inadequate.
modes.example: cannot be regarded as adequate to prove a<< definite>> cause-and-effect relationship.

modes.label: Uncertain whether related
modes.description: The verb is or were after 'whether the occurrence of X', ahead of related or due to.
modes.example: It is uncertain whether the occurrence of HSTCL<< is>> related to use of a TNF blocker

modes.label: No link or not established
modes.description: Small words like no or a before link or causal relationship in denials.
modes.example: however,<< a>> causal relationship has not been established.

card.writes: It pushes the model to continue with words about causes and influence, such as causal, caus and influence.
card.plain: It fires on the words leading into a statement about whether one thing causes another, usually when the link is doubtful.
